[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Action predictions fail when preconditions are not verified. Movement: do not assume a forward or direct move toward a target will succeed; first check that the path is clear and, if an obstacle blocks it, navigate around it, remove it, or replan. Pickup: do not assume pickup will succeed; first verify the target object exists, is visible/reachable, and is within the robot's current location or near enough; if not, navigate to it first. Place: do not attempt to place until the robot is confirmed to be holding the target object; perform and confirm a successful pick first. General lesson: before every action, validate its preconditions (path clear, object present/reachable, holding state correct), and when a prediction fails, diagnose which precondition was violated and replan rather than repeating the same command.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Inspect the current state and target: identify the object, destination, and any obstacles. 2. For movement, check the intended path and current location; if blocked, navigate around or remove the obstacle, or choose an alternate route. 3. For pickup, verify the object exists, is visible/reachable, and is near the robot; if not, move to its location. 4. Attempt pickup and confirm the robot is holding the object. 5. For placement/delivery, confirm holding state, then place the object at the destination. 6. After each action, verify the expected outcome; if it fails, identify the violated precondition and replan before retrying.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
